text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment options include a multi-step approach of lifestyle changes, oral or injectable medications, and sometimes insulin therapy or surgery to manage blood sugar levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: a multi-step approach of lifestyle changes, oral or injectable medications, and sometimes insulin therapy or surgery to manage blood sugar levels

list.snippet: Diet: Follow a balanced eating plan focused on lean proteins, non-starchy vegetables, high-fiber foods, and healthy fats (such as the Mediterranean or DASH diet).
Physical Activity: Get regular exercise to help the body use insulin more effectively.
Weight Management: Achieving weight management significantly improves blood sugar control and insulin sensitivity.
Biguanides (Metformin): Usually the first medicine prescribed; it lowers glucose production in the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.
Sulfonylureas: (e.g., glipizide, glimepiride, glyburide) Stimulate the pancreas to produce more insulin.
TZDs (Thiazolidinediones): (e.g., pioglitazone, rosiglitazone) Help insulin work better in muscle and fat cells.
DPP-4 Inhibitors (Gliptins): (e.g., sitagliptin) Enhance incretin hormones to lower post-meal blood sugar.
SGLT2 Inhibitors: Help the kidneys remove excess glucose through the urine while offering heart and kidney protection.
Meglitinides & Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors: Stimulate fast insulin release around mealtimes or slow carbohydrate breakdown.
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists & Dual GIP/GLP-1 Agonists: (e.g., tirzepatide, semaglutide) Injectable drugs that lower blood sugar, support weight management, and reduce cardiovascular risks.

Exogenous Insulin: Used if oral medications and lifestyle changes no longer keep blood sugar in target range, or if initial blood sugar/A1C levels are elevated. It can be long-acting, short-acting, or pre-mixed, delivered via pens, syringes, or pumps.
Bariatric (Weight Loss) Surgery: Can help eligible individuals manage or achieve remission of type 2 diabetes.
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs): Wearable sensors that track blood sugar trends in real time.
